The marginal 32 px epoch (~0.85 s) buys about 0.7-1.0 pp, so a per-step cut is worth keeping only if its pp-per-second rate falls below that measured line. Every past 'better than the epoch line' verdict depends on this slope, which has only been estimated from an SGD pair and one noisy Muon pair.

Prediction: on the E021 recipe at 9.25, 10.25 and 11.25 32-px-equivalent epochs (low-res share fixed), with 2 internal salts per point, the accuracy-vs-time slope is 0.6-1.2 pp/s, and the 9.25 to 10.25 step adds >=0.5 pp. Every per-step cut is then re-scored against this line.

Prediction: a lighter loss filter on E021 (drop the 10-15% lowest-loss examples, only in the last third of training) plus about +0.5 epoch reaches a 3-seed mean >=0.755 at lower time than E021. Equivalently, its pp/s cost sits below the N1a slope. If it does not, H1.6 is refuted.

Prediction: on E021 at batch 1536, scaling the Muon lr by 0.8x and 1.25x (momentum fixed) moves the 3-seed mean by >=0.25 pp in one direction (2 salts each). This means the inherited Hiverge lr is not at the optimum for this net.

FixRes-style mechanism: low-res training costs little final accuracy because the closing 32 px phase only needs to re-fit BN running statistics and the head to the test resolution. With fast BN running-stat momentum (as in Fable and airbench94_muon), that phase can be shorter. Part of E020's gain over E015 may come from this, beyond seed luck.

Prediction: on E021, raise the BN running-stat momentum to about 0.4-0.5 (PyTorch convention; first check the incumbent's value) and move 1 epoch from 32 px to 24 px at fixed total epochs. This cuts mean time by >=3%, and the 3-seed mean stays >=0.755 (2 salts).

Prediction: in the 24 px phase, step cost per image is lower, so Muon's fixed ~2 ms per step is a larger share. Raising the batch to 2048-3072 in the low-res phase only (Muon lr scaled by sqrt of the batch ratio, separate graph captured in build) cuts low-res phase time by >=8% and total time by >=2%. The 3-seed mean stays within noise (2 salts).

Prediction (resolution-tied regularization): on E021 at fixed epochs, label smoothing ~0.2 and crop translation scaled to 24 px during the low-res phase, with ls 0.3 at 32 px, raises the 3-seed mean by >=0.15 pp (2 salts). That margin would allow ~0.2-0.3 fewer epochs.

Prediction: training the whitening-conv bias only in the first ~1-3 epochs and then stopping backward before the 32x32 whitening stage (a second CUDA graph captured in build) cuts ms/step by >=2% in the later epochs and total time by >=1.5%. The 3-seed mean stays within noise.

Prediction: cutting Newton-Schulz from 3 steps to 2 (with retuned quintic coefficients or Turbo-Muon preconditioning) saves about 0.3 ms/step, cutting train time by >=1%. The 3-seed mean stays within noise (2 salts). Applying weight renormalization every k steps (Hiverge: 2 rising to 17) instead of every step adds a further >=0.3%.

Prediction (winner's curse): evaluating the E021 incumbent on dev seeds 3-12, outside the official run command, gives a 10-seed mean 0.05-0.3 pp below its 3-seed mean of 0.7552 and a per-seed std of 0.2-0.35 pp. If the dev mean is <0.754, further epoch trims are off-limits.

The local score may not carry over to official judging: an A100 80GB PCIe (power-capped, with different clock behaviour from the SXM) and a 40-seed mean. Time wins that remove work (steps, pixels, NS iterations, backward passes) carry over roughly proportionally. Wins under ~2% that depend on kernel scheduling or launch overhead may shrink or reverse, so they should be treated as provisional.
new.source: review; search:abdullah-athar PR #3 (SXM vs PCIe note)

new.statement: Mechanism: a power-capped PCIe A100 lowers sustained clocks under the compute-bound conv kernels more than under the launch- or memory-bound parts. Conv-FLOP cuts (resizing, depth cuts) therefore carry over at least proportionally, while overhead cuts (CUDA graphs, fused updates) carry over proportionally less. Rank candidate changes by work removed when local deltas are within ~2%.

structured_output.summary: The tree now treats noise as the main problem, matching the review. H4 is rewritten as a decision/selection-noise hypothesis, the salt replicate (H4.1.1) is retargeted onto E021, and a winner's-curse dev-seed prediction is added (N9). Verdicts inside the ~0.2 pp band are downgraded: H1.3.1 and H1.7.3 to inconclusive, H4.2 to inconclusive. H1.1.2 is changed to refuted, because 'supports' rested on one clause of the prediction. The SGD branch H1.1 and H1.7.4 are retired; H1.7.5 is retired because the schedule already decays only to ~0.07x. H1.5 is set to inconclusive: its evidence was misfiled and the E008 record is inconsistent. H1.7 is lowered to 0.3 and rewritten as an untuned Muon lr/momentum hypothesis, since E016 shows the SGD-era parts do useful work. H2.4.1 is refuted by the profiler (23% non-conv time) and H2.4 is rewritten around conv efficiency in the high-resolution stage. Marked supported: H2.3 (resizing, -4.2% time), H2.4.2 and H2.5/H2.5.1 (CUDA graph, -3%). H3 and H3.2.x are supported and closed as exhausted. New nodes: a wide-span epoch-slope measurement (N1/N1a) to replace the unmeasured ~1 pp/s line; a lighter loss filter to settle H1.6; a Muon lr sweep; FixRes/fast-BN-momentum, low-res batch-size and resolution-tied regularization children under H2.3; whitening-bias freezing (N7); NS 3 to 2 plus periodic renormalization (N8); and a new Lvl1 on transfer to the PCIe judging GPU and the 40-seed mean (N10). Suggested order: salt replicates and dev seeds on E021, then the wide-span slope, then NS=2 and whitening-bias freezing, then the resizing-schedule sweep.
